insights.concise_text: The character-level encoder-decoder framework addresses the challenging automatic mapping of natural language questions to KB queries by significantly improving performance over state-of-the-art word-level neural models.

triple.subject: character-level encoder-decoder framework
triple.object: automatic mapping of natural language questions to KB queries

insights.concise_text: Character-level modeling is chosen to make the model robust to unseen KB entries because it has been previously shown to generalize well to new words not seen during training.

triple.subject: character-level modeling
triple.object: unseen KB entries

insights.concise_text: The semantic relevance function addresses the scale problem of millions of entities and thousands of predicates by avoiding a large output layer in the decoder.

triple.subject: semantic relevance function
triple.object: millions of entities and thousands of predicates

insights.concise_text: The model trained only on SimpleQuestions training questions, which cover about 24% of words in entity aliases on the test set, achieves 70.9% accuracy in the Freebase2M setting and 70.3% accuracy in the Freebase5M setting.

triple.subject: character-level encoder-decoder model
triple.object: 70.9% accuracy in the Freebase2M setting and 70.3% accuracy in the Freebase5M setting

insights.concise_text: The character-level model uses no data augmentation unlike MemNNs, and its 1.2M parameters contrast with the word-level model's 19.9M parameters and best SQ accuracy of 53.9%.

triple.subject: character-level model
triple.object: word-level model

insights.concise_text: The OOV problem from word-level embeddings explains why previous approaches rely on significant data augmentation from sources such as Paralex, which contains 18 million question-paraphrase pairs scraped from WikiAnswers.

triple.subject: out-of-vocabulary (OOV) problem
triple.object: reliance on significant data augmentation from sources such as Paralex

insights.concise_text: The model's semantic relevance function is implemented as cosine similarity between decoder hidden states and KB entry embeddings to avoid an output layer with millions of nodes.

triple.subject: cosine-similarity metric: $cos(x_1, x_2)$
triple.object: an output layer with millions of nodes

insights.concise_text: The model decodes a KB query consisting of exactly the topic entity and predicate by selecting the most likely (entity, predicate) pair from generated candidate entities and predicates.

triple.subject: model
triple.object: the most likely (entity, predicate) pair

insights.concise_text: The severe OOV issue for entities is supported by SimpleQuestions having only 10,843 of the 45,335 unique words in entity aliases present in the train set and by the word-level model predicting only 45% of entities accurately.

triple.subject: SimpleQuestions train-test vocabulary gap
triple.object: word-level entity prediction to 45%

insights.concise_text: In random-sampling experiments with 200 entities and predicates as noise samples, character-level models achieve 96.6% accuracy in predicting the correct entity while word-level models predict 45% of entities accurately.

triple.subject: character-level models
triple.object: word-level models on entity prediction

insights.concise_text: The attention distribution peaks at empty spaces because the blue and green curves visualize attention over question characters when generating the entity and predicate.

triple.subject: the attention distribution peaks at empty spaces
triple.object: the blue and green curves visualizing attention over question characters when generating the entity and predicate

insights.concise_text: The conclusion that character-level modeling gives a compact model that is robust to unseen entities is evidenced by identifying phrenology, whose English aliases were never seen in training.

triple.subject: identifying phrenology, whose English aliases were never seen in training
triple.object: the conclusion that character-level modeling gives a compact model that is robust to unseen entities

insights.concise_text: Because the blue curve is entity attention and the green curve is predicate attention, entity attention distributions are usually less sharp and span longer portions of words than predicate attention distributions.

triple.subject: the blue curve
triple.object: the green curve in spanning longer portions of words

insights.concise_text: The hidden state of the LSTM encoder at a space likely summarizes content before that space, explaining why attention distribution typically peaks at empty spaces.

triple.subject: the hidden state of the LSTM encoder at a space likely summarizes content before that space
triple.object: the attention distribution typically peaks at empty spaces

insights.concise_text: The attention model's capability to attend disjoint regions of the question supports the proposed model not needing to make a hard categorization between predicate and entity mentions.

triple.subject: the attention model's capability to attend disjoint regions of the question
triple.object: the proposed model not needing to make a hard categorization between predicate and entity mentions
